traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 82 records annotated as flowering (May 41, Jun 37, Jul 4); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, May and June. The Seed Manual (Physocarpus chapter, printed p. 790) gives April to June.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 37 plant-years at 8 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Jan 5, Feb 1, May 1, Jun 11, Jul 12, Aug 18, Sep 18, Oct 19, Nov 13, Dec 7); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, June to December. The Seed Manual (Physocarpus chapter, printed p. 790) gives no month for its dry follicles, and says some may stay on until the end of winter.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944), as Physocarpus capitatus: a shrub with erect or suckering branches, 1 m to 5 m high.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Jepson (1925), as P. capitatus: leaves 2.5 cm to 7.6 cm long (converted from inches).

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a shrub of arching stems with shredding bark, three-lobed toothed leaves and round heads of small white flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 2.8 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: glossy mid-green leaves; white flower heads; peeling brown bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: round heads of small inflated follicles, green turning reddish. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: white heads in May and June; follicles reddish from July, dry and brown into the winter. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): shreddy bark peeling in thin strips; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): white flowers about 1 cm across with about 30 red-tipped stamens, from pink buds, in dense rounded clusters that open from the outside in over about two weeks (as in the related P. opulifolius). From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five white petals between five sepals on a floral cup, thirty stamens and a pistil of three carpels, from the characters of Rosaceae and Physocarpus by the rules at the flowering plants.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.opening.note: Days from the first flower of a cluster opening to its last: about two weeks, as described for P. opulifolius.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.bud_look.note: Pink buds, a third of the flower's width, as described for the species.
